question_text: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. Given that $P(A \cup B) = 0.63$ and $P(B) = 0.36$, find $P(A)$.

subparts.stem: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. Given that $P(A \cup B) = 0.63$ and $P(B) = 0.36$, find $P(A)$.
subparts.solution:
$$\text{P}(A \cup B) = \text{P}(A) + \text{P}(B) - \text{P}(A \cap B)$$
$$\therefore 0.63 = \text{P}(A) + 0.36 - \text{P}(A)\text{P}(B) \quad \{A \text{ and } B \text{ are independent}\}$$
$$\therefore 0.27 = \text{P}(A) - 0.36 \times \text{P}(A)$$
$$\therefore 0.27 = 0.64 \times \text{P}(A)$$
$$\therefore \text{P}(A) = \frac{0.27}{0.64} \approx 0.422$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: If two events $A$ and $B$ are independent, $\text{P}(A \cap B) = \text{P}(A) \times \text{P}(B)$.
step_by_step: Substitute $\text{P}(A \cap B) = \text{P}(A) \times 0.36$ into the addition rule.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing independence with mutually exclusive events (assuming $\text{P}(A \cap B) = 0$).
